## Experience

- Swarms, Agent Engineer Intern, remote, since October 2026. 44 merged PRs as of November 6, 2026, 32 code and 12 docs, into an open-source Python multi-agent framework. 6 of them merged over competing PRs. Added SMTP/IMAP and AgentMail email channels and a GraphWorkflow error policy, and removed 600+ lines of dead code. CronJob.stop() failed with "cannot join current thread" when a job stopped itself, and left its task scheduled. Fixed that and a restart race, with 6 sleep-free regression tests checked against 16 deliberately broken versions of the method.
- Sigma Lambda Beta Education Foundation, Software Engineer, remote, since May 2025. Maintains an ASP.NET/C# and MySQL donation portal with 27K+ donations and Authorize.NET payments. Combined payment types with an idempotent SQL migration that has a rollback, tested against 24 scenarios and a production snapshot. Moved the District model to Region across 30+ files, which fixed 2 crashes and halved the region report's database round-trips.
- BNY, Tech Lead at the Sophomore Summit, May to July 2025. Led a 5-person team in a mock-IPO coding challenge and presented the team's Python share-allocation algorithm to senior engineers.
- Domus Care Solutions, Software Engineer Intern, Weston, FL, May to July 2024. Built a Java Swing report builder for patient records, and automated Google Sheets dashboards that saved analysts 8+ hours of manual sorting a week.
- Florida International University, B.S. Computer Science, graduating summer 2027. VP of Finance of FIU's Sigma Lambda Beta chapter, and its president in 2024–2025.

## Projects

- [MomentumX](https://github.com/Kpeguero16/MomentumX): A tokenized stock trading platform on Solana. Backend lead on a team of four. Built the FastAPI transaction layer. It checks each wallet-signed trade against its quote, co-signs it and submits it idempotently, so a dropped connection never loses or doubles a trade. Python, FastAPI, SQLite, Solana, pytest.
- [QuantSim](https://github.com/Kpeguero16/quantsim): A paper trading and backtesting platform built as six Go microservices with 600+ tests. About 2,000 orders/s at 64 ms p99 with 100 concurrent clients. Row locks stop double-spends: 500 concurrent orders against a balance for 10 fill exactly 10. Backtests run at about 5M bars a second. Go, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, React.
- [HermeΣ](https://usehermes.online/): A Slack app that turns weekly chapter minutes into summaries, task lists and Google Calendar events. A diff-based sync keeps the calendar matched to the minutes, and E-Board members can ask a Slack agent about the calendar in plain English. In use by 20+ members across 2 chapters. n8n, Python, Slack API, Google Calendar API, Linux VPS. Source: https://github.com/Kpeguero16/Hermes
- [MedVoyage](https://kpeguero16.github.io/MedVoyage/): A medical-diagnosis web app the team built front to back in a weekend, with parallax-scroll animations. HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Git. Source: https://github.com/Kpeguero16/MedVoyage
- [365 Days](https://github.com/Kpeguero16/365Days): A digital anniversary album with date-gated entry. A Node.js pipeline renames, compresses and tracks 500+ media files, 1.3 GB, through Git LFS. 100 Lighthouse scores for performance and accessibility. HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, Git LFS.

## How Khalil works

Small changes, each with proof.

1. Pick: choose changes small enough to review in one sitting.
2. Reproduce: write the check that fails on master.
3. Build: make the change in its own worktree. Coding agents do the typing, and Khalil reads every line.
4. Prove: the same check passes on the branch, and the module's tests still pass.
5. Ship: open a PR that states the problem, the fix and the evidence.
